say.en: A camera flash charges a capacitor for a few seconds and then empties it into the lamp in a thousandth of a second. Capacitors store charge and energy. In this lesson: Define capacitance and its unit.
Use C equals epsilon 0 epsilon rA over d and W equals one half CV squared.
Combine capacitors in series and parallel and read their codes.

body.en: A capacitor is two conductors separated by an insulator (dielectric). Its *capacitance* is the charge stored per volt: $C = Q/V$, measured in farads; practical values are in µF, nF and pF. For parallel plates $C = ε_0 ε_r A/d$. The energy stored is $W = ½CV^2$.
body.kn: ಡೈಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಿಕ್‌ನಿಂದ ಬೇರ್ಪಟ್ಟ ಎರಡು ವಾಹಕಗಳೇ ಧಾರಕ. ಧಾರಕತೆ C = Q/V, ಏಕಮಾನ ಫ್ಯಾರಡ್. ಸಮಾಂತರ ಫಲಕಗಳಿಗೆ C = ε0εrA/d. ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿತ ಶಕ್ತಿ W = ½CV².

Its capacitance is the charge stored per volt: C equals Q over V, measured in farads; practical values are in µF, nF and pF. For parallel plates C equals epsilon _0 epsilon _r A over d. title.en: On the board: Capacitors and combinations

say.en: A capacitor is two conducting plates with an insulator between them. Charge plus Q collects on one plate and minus Q on the other.
In parallel the plate areas add, so the capacitances add. In series the same charge sits on each, and the reciprocals add.
Example: 4 and 12 microfarads. In parallel they make 16. In series, product over sum, they make 3 microfarads.
Small capacitors carry a code in picofarads. 104 means 10 followed by four zeros picofarads, which is 0.1 microfarad.
On the board: Capacitors and combinations.

title.en: Capacitors in series and in parallel

narration.en: In parallel the capacitances add and each capacitor has the full voltage. In series the same charge sits on each capacitor, the voltage divides (more across the smaller one) and the total is less than the smallest. The bars show the charge on each.
narration.kn: ಸಮಾಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ ಧಾರಕತೆಗಳು ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ, ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಪೂರ್ಣ ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್. ಸರಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದರಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ಆವೇಶ, ಚಿಕ್ಕದರ ಮೇಲೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್. ಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳು ಆವೇಶ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Paper, mica, ceramic, polyester and electrolytic *capacitors* differ in dielectric. Electrolytic capacitors give large values in a small size but are polarised: the + lead must go to the higher potential. Variable (gang) capacitors tune radios. A capacitor is specified by capacitance, working voltage and tolerance. Small capacitors use a code in picofarads: 104 means 10 × 10⁴ pF = 0.1 µF.
body.kn: ಕಾಗದ, ಮೈಕಾ, ಸೆರಾಮಿಕ್, ವಿದ್ಯುದ್ವಿಭಜ್ಯ ಧಾರಕಗಳು ಡೈಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಿಕ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಭಿನ್ನ. ವಿದ್ಯುದ್ವಿಭಜ್ಯ ಧಾರಕಕ್ಕೆ ಧ್ರುವೀಯತೆ ಇದೆ. ಸಂಕೇತ 104 = 0.1 µF.

body.en: In parallel, capacitances add: $C_p = C_1 + C_2$, because the plate areas add. In *series*, $1/C_s = 1/C_1 + 1/C_2$; every capacitor carries the same charge. This is the opposite of resistors.

problem.en: A parallel-plate capacitor has plate area 0.02 m², separation 1 mm and a dielectric with εᵣ = 5. Find C (ε₀ = 8.854 × 10⁻¹² F/m).

say.en: Let us solve this together. A parallel-plate capacitor has plate area 0.02 square metres, separation 1 millimetre and a dielectric with epsilon r equals 5. Find C (epsilon 0 equals 8.854 times 10 to the power minus 12 F over m).
C equals epsilon 0 epsilon rA over d equals 8.854 times 10 to the power minus 12 times 5 times 0.02 divided by 0.001.
= 8.854 times 10 to the power minus 12 times 100 equals 8.854 times 10 to the power minus 10 F.
is approximately 885 picofarads.

problem.en: Capacitors of 4 µF and 12 µF are in series across 100 V. Find C_s and the charge on each.

steps.en: Q = C_s V = 3 µF × 100 V = 300 µC on each capacitor.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Capacitors of 4 µF and 12 µF are in series across 100 V. Find C_s and the charge on each.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Capacitors of 4 microfarads and 12 microfarads are in series across 100 volts. Find C s and the charge on each.
C s equals 4 times 12/4 plus 12 equals 3 microfarads.
Q equals C s V equals 3 microfarads times 100 volts equals 300 µC on each capacitor.
Check: V 1 equals 300 over 4 equals 75 volts, V 2 equals 300 over 12 equals 25 volts; 75 plus 25 equals 100 volts.
So the answer is 3 microfarads; 300 µC.
